title: Noncomputability of the unary halting language
statement: Let $H$ be the set of natural numbers $m$ for which the machine with index given by the first component of the Cantor pairing decomposition of $m$ halts on input given by its second component. The language consisting of the all-true Boolean lists whose lengths belong to $H$ has no computable membership predicate.
